resources.string: Remove all hidden data from a photo before you share it.
Ready. Tap the button to strip metadata.
That share was not a content link and was ignored.

On. Lossy photos are rebuilt from raw pixels, so nothing hidden can survive. HEIC stays HEIC where the device supports it. JPEG stays JPEG, and AVIF becomes JPEG, because MetaStrip does not encode AVIF. PNG, WebP, GIF and BMP are always rebuilt losslessly.

Off. JPEG, HEIC and AVIF keep their pixels and colour profile exactly as they are, so the picture looks identical. Only the metadata blocks are cut out. JPEGs shot sideways may lose their rotation. PNG, WebP, GIF and BMP are still rebuilt losslessly.

Re-encoding is the only way to be sure every piece of metadata is gone, including types this app does not know about.

With it off, MetaStrip cuts the known metadata blocks out of JPEG, HEIC and AVIF files and keeps the compressed pixels untouched. Your photo quality and colours stay exactly as they were, but:

• Unusual or hidden data inside the pixel stream cannot be detected.
• The colour profile is kept, so the picture still looks right. It names a colour space, not you.
• JPEGs shot sideways may appear sideways, because the rotation lives in the removed EXIF block. HEIC and AVIF keep their rotation.

PNG, WebP, GIF and BMP are lossless already and are always rebuilt from pixels.

Do you want to turn it off?
On. Saved files get a random 13 character name, like hwpn1dprea5c9.jpg, so the name gives nothing away.
Off. Saved files keep the original name with _clean added.
On. After a clean copy is saved, MetaStrip asks Android to delete the photo you picked. Android shows its own confirmation each time.
Off. The photo you picked is left alone and a clean copy is saved alongside it.

The clean copy is always written and checked first, so a failure cannot lose your photo. After that, MetaStrip asks Android to delete the original, and Android shows its own confirmation each time.

Deleting cannot be undone. The photo may still sit in your gallery's recently deleted folder for a while, but do not count on it.

Photos chosen with the system picker cannot be deleted at all, because Android only grants read access to them. Sharing a photo into MetaStrip from your gallery does allow it.

Turn this on?
That location does not allow lasting access. Pick a folder on device storage instead.
Go back to Pictures/MetaStrip and forget the custom folder.
EXIF, XMP, IPTC, ICC, thumbnails, comments and more.

Photos carry hidden data: where they were taken, when, with which phone, sometimes even the owner's name.

Lossless formats (PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP) are always decoded to raw pixels and written as a fresh lossless file. Nothing but pixels is written, so nothing hidden survives.

Lossy formats (JPEG, HEIC, AVIF) do the same by default. JPEG stays JPEG at quality 95, and HEIC stays HEIC on devices with an HEVC encoder. AVIF becomes JPEG, because MetaStrip does not encode AVIF. Turn off re-encoding in Settings to keep their compressed pixels byte for byte and remove only the metadata blocks: EXIF, XMP, IPTC, ICC profiles, thumbnails, comments and vendor blocks.

AVIF re-encoding needs Android 12 or newer. Lossless AVIF stripping works on any version.

The original file is never changed. A new copy is written to the save folder.
No permissions, no network, no data collected.

MetaStrip asks for no permissions. It uses the system photo picker to read the image you choose and the system folder picker or media library to save the result.\n\nThe app has no internet access. Nothing leaves your device. No analytics, no crash reporting, no accounts.
